# UTF-8

Encoding, decoding and validating UTF-8, and the limits of a Unicode scalar value.

<h2 id="max-scalar-value"><code>MaxScalarValue</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MaxScalarValue: uint32 = 0x10FFFF;
```

The largest Unicode scalar value.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L19)

<h2 id="first-surrogate"><code>FirstSurrogate</code></h2>

```rux
pub const FirstSurrogate: uint32 = 0xD800;
```

The first value of the surrogate range, which holds no scalar values.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L23)

<h2 id="last-surrogate"><code>LastSurrogate</code></h2>

```rux
pub const LastSurrogate: uint32 = 0xDFFF;
```

The last value of the surrogate range.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L27)

<h2 id="max-encoded-length"><code>MaxEncodedLength</code></h2>

```rux
pub const MaxEncodedLength: uint = 4;
```

The most bytes any one scalar value takes in UTF-8.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L31)

<h2 id="decoded-scalar"><code>DecodedScalar</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct DecodedScalar {
    pub scalar: char32;
    pub width: uint;
}
```

One scalar value decoded from UTF-8, with the number of bytes it occupied.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L51)

**Fields**

| Name     | Type     | Description                                   |
| -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `scalar` | `char32` | The Unicode scalar value.                     |
| `width`  | `uint`   | How many bytes it occupied, one through four. |

<h2 id="utf8-failure"><code>Utf8Failure</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct Utf8Failure {
    pub reason: Utf8Error;
    pub index: uint;
}
```

Where and why a byte sequence stopped being well-formed UTF-8.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L60)

**Fields**

| Name     | Type        | Description                                                |
| -------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |

| `index`  | `uint`      | The offset of the byte that starts the offending sequence. |

<h2 id="is-scalar-value"><code>IsScalarValue</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsScalarValue(value: uint32) -> bool
```

Whether `value` is a Unicode scalar value: at most [`MaxScalarValue`](/docs/api/text/utf8#max-scalar-value), and not a surrogate half.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L72)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type     | Description         |
| ------- | -------- | ------------------- |
| `value` | `uint32` | the value to act on |

**Returns**: whether the value is a Unicode scalar value, which excludes the surrogates

<h2 id="encoded-length"><code>EncodedLength</code></h2>

```rux
pub func EncodedLength(scalar: char32) -> uint
```

How many bytes `scalar` takes in UTF-8, or zero when it is not a scalar value.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L81)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type     | Description              |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `scalar` | `char32` | the Unicode scalar value |

**Returns**: how many bytes the scalar's encoding occupies, one through four

<h2 id="is-continuation"><code>IsContinuation</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsContinuation(byte: char8) -> bool
```

Whether `byte` is a continuation byte, the `10xxxxxx` shape every byte after a leading one has.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L94)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type    | Description |
| ------ | ------- | ----------- |
| `byte` | `char8` | the byte    |

**Returns**: whether the byte continues a sequence rather than starting one

<h2 id="encode"><code>Encode</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Encode(scalar: char32, into: var char8[..]) -> uint ! Utf8Error
```

Writes `scalar` into `into` as UTF-8 and reports how many bytes it took.
`into` is borrowed mutably and must have room for the encoding — at most [`MaxEncodedLength`](/docs/api/text/utf8#max-encoded-length) bytes. Fails with
`InvalidStart` for a value that is not a scalar value, and `Truncated` when there is not enough room; nothing is
written in either case.
Cannot allocate. Runs in constant time.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L107)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type            | Description              |
| -------- | --------------- | ------------------------ |
| `scalar` | `char32`        | the Unicode scalar value |
| `into`   | `var char8[..]` | receives the bytes       |

**Returns**: how many bytes were written, or why none were

<h2 id="decode-at"><code>DecodeAt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func DecodeAt(bytes: char8[..], index: uint) -> DecodedScalar ! Utf8Error
```

Decodes the scalar value starting at `index`, reporting it and how many bytes it occupied.
`bytes` is borrowed. On a failure the caller decides what to do — a decoder replacing bad input with U+FFFD
advances one byte and carries on, and one rejecting it stops.
Cannot allocate. Runs in constant time.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L190)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |
| `index` | `uint`      | the byte offset     |

**Returns**: the scalar and its width, or why the bytes there are not one

<h2 id="validate"><code>Validate</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Validate(bytes: char8[..]) -> ! Utf8Failure
```

Whether `bytes` is well-formed UTF-8 from end to end, reporting where it first is not.
`bytes` is borrowed. A failure carries the index of the byte that starts the offending sequence.
Cannot allocate. Runs in time proportional to the length.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L227)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |

**Returns**: nothing when every byte is part of a valid sequence, or where and why the first one is not

<h2 id="is-boundary"><code>IsBoundary</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsBoundary(bytes: char8[..], index: uint) -> bool
```

Whether `index` is where a scalar value starts, and so a place a string may be cut.
The length counts as a boundary, so the end of a string is always a legal cut. An index past the length is not.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L242)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |
| `index` | `uint`      | the byte offset     |

**Returns**: whether `index` falls between two scalar values rather than inside one

<h2 id="count-scalars"><code>CountScalars</code></h2>

```rux
pub func CountScalars(bytes: char8[..]) -> uint
```

How many scalar values `bytes` holds, assuming it is well-formed.
Counts leading bytes, which is one per scalar value in well-formed UTF-8. Bytes that are not well-formed give a
count that means nothing; [`Validate`](/docs/api/text/utf8#validate) is what answers whether they are.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L255)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |

**Returns**: how many scalar values the bytes encode

<h2 id="boundary-at-or-below"><code>BoundaryAtOrBelow</code></h2>

```rux
pub func BoundaryAtOrBelow(bytes: char8[..], index: uint) -> uint
```

The index of the scalar boundary at or below `index`.
An index inside a sequence is walked back to the start of that sequence, which is what a caller cutting at an
arbitrary byte offset needs. An index at or past the length gives the length.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Utf8.rux#L274)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |
| `index` | `uint`      | the byte offset     |

**Returns**: the largest boundary at or below `index`, so a truncation splits nothing
